findings: Owner request 2026-11-08: practice long questions for Chapter 1 in the style of the Board long question (the owner's Board papers were a style demo only: a 5-mark theory question with a 3-mark numerical). Written from the chapter; not printed in the book and no past-paper question is copied. 26 questions numbered 1-26 (owner: plain numbers, no a/b), odd numbers theory (5 marks) and even numbers numericals (3 marks).

Coverage: base and derived quantities with the measurement steps and Table 1.1; SI and its conventions; prefixes and powers of ten; absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty; significant figures (counting, rounding, multiplying/dividing, adding/subtracting); precision and accuracy; digital instruments and the thumb rules (mean deviation, periodic uncertainty); total uncertainty (sums, quotients, power factor); dimensions, homogeneity, derivation of a formula (centripetal force), limitations of dimensional analysis and of significant figures; derived and additional SI units (Table 1.2); E = mc² (Do You Know?).

Theory answers follow the chapter's own words and examples. Numerical parts are self-check questions solved step by step (steps + final answer) with values changed from the chapter's examples; every number was recomputed in Python. Two answers carry an answer_table (Tables 1.1 and 1.2).
Every question carries a book_ref (topic id and exact words of that topic's English lesson); refs_verify.py reports 0 problems.
The Roman Urdu file has the same questions, order and book_refs; each prompt keeps the English question with the Roman Urdu meaning in brackets; 5 Wazahat callouts (Roman Urdu only).
Book errors avoided: the 0.5 A misprint (0.05 A used, Wazahat explains), the µ symbol for the atomic mass unit (u used, Wazahat explains) and the cm unit of area (cm² used).
Drafts for the academic review (second-person review before publication).
